1.why: The UI uses a clean sans-serif typeface with adequate letter and line spacing across all screens.

2.why: Instructions use sentence case without italics or all-caps, though some info boxes contain multi-line text blocks.

3.why: Layouts are single-column, responsive, and clearly readable at mobile width in every screenshot.

4.why: Most instructions are short and plain, such as 'Enter the six-digit code generated during setup'.

5.why: No explicit example format is shown for expected inputs like the authenticator secret or recovery codes beyond placeholders.

6.why: Users can proceed without reading logs, but demo info boxes and growing log panels add non-trivial text on several steps.

7.why: The long setup secret and backup codes are displayed as plain text without a copy button, so manual selection is required.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent scan option is offered; authenticator setup is manual-entry only.

9.why: Standard email/phone inputs may allow autofill, but OTP and recovery-code fields show no explicit password-manager support.

10.why: Page titles and prominent blue primary buttons clearly indicate the current step and main action on every screen.

11.why: Each step focuses on one primary task, though secondary actions like 'Get a simulation challenge' appear alongside.

12.why: Green confirmation banners and status messages state what happened and the next step after key actions.

13.why: Users can re-request challenges, generate replacement codes, and navigate back without apparent penalty.

14.why: No error messages are shown in the screenshots, so problem-and-fix guidance cannot be verified.

15.why: No countdown timers or reading time limits are visible on any step; code entry appears untimed.
